question.text: A lift ascends with constant acceleration <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>a</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></math> , then with constant velocity and finally, it stops under constant retardation <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>a</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></math> . If total distance ascended by the lift is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>7</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math>, in a total time of the journey is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>8</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi></math>. Find the time (in second) for which lift moves with constant velocity.
